analysis.title: Across the Americas: Elections paint the country blue and the market red
key_insights: Midterm results are as much a rebuke of Republicans as an embrace of Democrats. Democrats are positioned to control both the House and the Senate in January 2027, with Republicans down 41 House seats and 7 Senate seats at the time of writing.

October payrolls rose 165k with unemployment at 4.2% (higher participation). Wages rose 0.4% m/m and September was revised up to 0.3%. Natixis reads this as a stable labor market, not a hot one, and not a concern for the Fed.

Next week's CPI matters more for Fed rates than the jobs data. Headline CPI is expected to ease to 0.3% m/m from 0.6% and core to 0.2% from 0.3%. No y/y figure exists for October because the 2025 shutdown prevented price collection that month.

September JOLTS job openings rose to 7.5m from 7.2m, over 300k above consensus. The openings rate rose to 4.5% and quits to 2.1%. The vacancies-to-unemployed ratio rose to 1.06, but wage and ECI measures do not look inflationary.

ISM Manufacturing rose to 55.5 in October from 54.5, its tenth straight month of expansion. Production rose to 59.0, the highest since November 2021. The prices paid index fell 2.7 points to 75.2, so prices moderated but did not fall.

ISM Services edged down to 54.5 from 54.9, slightly below the 54.8 expected. Underlying activity softened more than the headline suggests. The prices index fell to 73.0, employment rose to 51.4, and a respondent quote summed it up as 'Overall demand is sluggish.'

Natixis attributes the post-election market reaction to three factors. A Democratic Congress could block or end the Iran War, push back on the tariff regime, and slow the data center buildout (less crowding out of the long end of the UST curve). Natixis calls two of the three still theoretical, since the new Congress does not sit for two months.

A data-center-driven tech selloff on Thursday sparked a flight-to-quality rally in USTs. Natixis cannot argue with the move given Warsh's focus on financial conditions, but cannot predict the next 10% equity move.

Natixis took profit on its long 2yr UST trade, entered at 4.88% and closed at 4.60% for +28bp, and also unwound receive 10s on 5s10s30s for +5bp. It sees yields across the curve at strong support and would prefer buying a pullback. It stays bullish the long end over the medium term but sees the rally as extended near term, a view reinforced by the NFP report.

12m forward Fed pricing has fallen to about 45bps of hikes, nearly 50bps off the highs in under a month. Natixis Economics still calls for one more hike this cycle. A lingering Iran War, a hawkish Fed, a strong job market and a lot of data before the December FOMC make removing more Fed pricing harder from here.
Natixis would scale into long 10s between 5.10% and 5.20% and wants 10s back at 5% or above. It does not rule out a 25bp retrace of the roughly 60bp rally of the past month.

Brazil: the BCB held Selic at 13.75% as expected, citing worse inflation expectations and growth risks. Natixis expects another pause in December. The path depends on fiscal clarity under Lula 4.0, where deterioration could force hikes and credible improvement could allow cuts.

Colombia: BanRep held at 12.25% as expected, with inflation above 6% and El Niño and elevated expectations as upside risks. Natixis puts a 55% probability on one more hike to a 12.50% terminal rate. BanRep will buy and sterilize $2bn from the government, separate from its plan to accumulate $4bn through options.

Mexico: Banxico cut 25bps to 6.25% in a 3-2 vote, which Natixis and most analysts did not expect. Forward guidance signals a one-off cut and an extended hold, so Natixis sees 6.25% as a floor. Natixis questions the output-gap rationale given a weaker MXN past 18.00, Q3 GDP of 0.90% and inflation expectations nearer 4.0%.

Natixis reads the Banxico decision as weighting growth over the inflation target, possibly with fiscal relief for the Finance Ministry in mind. It says the implied target looks like 4.0% rather than 3.0% and will adjust its survey inflation expectations accordingly.

tension_points.bull_case: A Democratic Congress can push back on tariffs and the Iran War, a slower data center buildout reduces crowding out of the long end, and the tech-driven flight to quality supports USTs. Natixis stays bullish the long end over the medium term.
tension_points.bear_case: The rally of roughly 60bp in a month came too fast and at least two of the three rationales are still theoretical. There is also a hawkish Fed, a strong job market, a lingering Iran War and yields at strong support levels.
tension_points.what_invalidates: 10yr yields sitting at weekly support near 4.846% and a retrace of about 25bps of the rally, with Natixis wanting 10s back at 5% or above before scaling in.
